etymologies.heading: Etymology
paragraphs: From Middle English bristil, bristel, brustel, from Old English bristl, byrst, *brystl, *byrstel, from Proto-West Germanic *burstilu, diminutive of Proto-West Germanic *bursti, from Proto-Germanic *burstiz (compare Dutch borstel, German Borste (“boar's bristle”), Icelandic burst), from Proto-Indo-European *bʰr̥stís (compare Middle Irish brostaid (“to goad, spur”), Latin fastīgium (“top”), Polish barszcz (“hogweed”)).
senses: A stiff or coarse hair on a nonhuman mammal or on a plant.
A chaeta: an analogous filament on arthropods, annelids, or other animals.
(intransitive) To rise or stand erect, like bristles.
(intransitive, usually with with) To abound, to be covered with, or to have an abundance of, something, especially something jutting out.
